package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to vulnerability fix (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a directory traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to craft archive files with file paths containing '../' or '../../'. When such archives are extracted using plexus-archiver, files can be written outside the intended extraction directory, potentially overwriting critical system files or placing malicious files in sensitive locations. This can lead to privilege escalation, persistence, or full system compromise if exploited.

execution_context.trigger: At archive extraction time, when a user or process extracts a crafted archive using plexus-archiver
execution_context.file_location: Within the file path metadata of entries inside the archive (e.g., zip, tar, gz files processed by plexus-archiver)

malicious_snippets.code_language: N/A (malicious file path within archive metadata, not source code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This file path, when included as an entry in an archive, causes plexus-archiver to write the extracted file outside the intended extraction directory by traversing up the directory tree. This can result in files being placed in arbitrary locations on the filesystem, including sensitive or system directories.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: File paths containing '../' or '../../' are a well-known indicator of directory traversal attacks. Their presence in archive file entries is suspicious because it enables writing files outside the extraction root, which is a common exploitation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal archive extraction should restrict all output to the specified extraction directory, sanitizing or rejecting any file paths that attempt to traverse directories. The vulnerable behavior allows traversal sequences to be processed, violating the expectation of containment and enabling files to be written to unintended locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some backup or restoration tools may use relative paths for restoring files to their original locations, but legitimate tools should never allow traversal outside the designated extraction root. Any use of '../' that escapes the extraction directory is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Archive file entries with '../' or '../../' in their paths
Extraction process does not sanitize or restrict traversal sequences in file paths
Files created or overwritten outside the intended extraction directory during archive extraction
Unexpected file system modifications in parent or system directories immediately after extraction

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious archive containing file entries with directory traversal paths such as '../../malicious_file.txt'.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim extracts the archive using plexus-archiver, initiating the vulnerable extraction process.

attack_chain.action: plexus-archiver processes the archive and writes files to disk, following the malicious traversal paths and placing files outside the intended extraction directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Critical files may be overwritten or new malicious files may be placed in sensitive locations on the filesystem.

attack_chain.action: Malicious files placed outside the intended directory may be executed or leveraged for further attacks, such as privilege escalation, persistence, or system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: attacker achieves system compromise, data manipulation, or persistent access.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction processes that result in file creation or modification outside the intended extraction directory
Presence of '../' or '../../' sequences in file paths within archive entries
Unexpected file system changes in parent or system directories immediately following archive extraction
file_indicators: Archive files containing file entries with '../' or '../../' in their paths
Files appearing or being modified outside the extraction directory after unpacking an archive
Unusual file creation events in system or user directories during archive extraction
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement pre-extraction scanning of archive files to detect file entries containing directory traversal sequences such as '../' or '../../'. Enforce path sanitization in extraction tools to prevent writing files outside the extraction directory. Monitor filesystem activity during and after archive extraction for unexpected file creation or modification events outside the intended directory. Alert or block extraction operations if traversal patterns are detected in archive metadata.
